Title: Hanes Men's Full Zip Ultimate Heavyweight Hoodie - With Poor Quality Defective Zipper
Review: Original Review, 2022.05.27, 1-StarNice material, too bad the zipper is very poor quality.  Attempting an exchange, and I'll modify this review depending on what's received as a replacement.  Unfortunately, the zipper on the jacket I received is non-functional.  It sticks and sometimes doesn't at all, and obviously wont last very long.  Too bad, otherwise its a nice jacket, but it's the worst zipper I've ever seen in my 50+ years of daily zippering.Update, 2022.05.30, 2-StarsPromptly received a replacement from Amazon.  The zipper is at least functional, but it probably won't last long.  You get what you pay for, with this hoodie.I like my hoodies extra big for layering.  Ordered a 3XL, and it runs short in length.  Much shorter than expected in length.  The front pockets are small and shallow.  I can barely fit my hands in them. At 6 feet tall of average build, 3XL sleeve length is almost too short, and the bottom hem is at my waist just above my hips.  It's more like XL from most other brands, as far as bottom hemline and sleeve length are concerned.  Otherwise about as roomy like a 2XL from most other clothiers.  Mens sizes.  A lot of lint too, like really, A LOT of LINT from washing cold and tumble dry on low.  Yep,  a bit of shrinkage too.  Obviously not preshrunk cotton.I suspect Hanes sizing is not consistent.  It has that feel of hurried cheap manufacture from a garment sweatshop.It's moderate weight.  Good for days when a light jacket is needed.  It's also good for layering under other clothes, but not so much over other clothing.Hanes quality has deteriorated drastically over time.  Once an established brand known for quality and durability, but alas those days are long past.About 30 years ago Hanes had some nice hoodies with quality material, and deep pockets, with zippers that lasted longer than the material.  They had a contract with the military for PT apparel, shorts, t-shirts, sweat pants, sweat shirts and hoodies. This hoodie is nowhere near that quality of yesteryear.I decided to keep this return replacement hoodie.  I expect it will need a new zipper after a year or two of wear in spring, fall and winter.  If the material actually holds up.I may just make one myself since no one seems to make quality mid to light weight cotton or hemp hoodies in relaxed, loose fitting XXL+ sizes.  A couple vendors make some excellent heavier weight warmer ones, like driduck for example, which I also wear.  However, they come in at a price point range of $60.00 to $120.00 or more, depending on merchandiser.  Amazon sells DriDuck for those seeking a heavier more durable hooded jacket.Too bad Hanes became a purveyor of cheaply made poor quality products guaranteed not to last more than a year or two.  I won't purchase Hanes again, unless they improve in quality and craft.  I'd prefer to pay more for something durable that will last and can handle several hundred machine wash cycles, rather than something that will fall apart after a few gentle hand washes followed by line dry.

Title: It's exactly what I wanted!
Review: I looked at almost 100 jackets in stores and websites before I decided on the Columbia Men’s Watertight II Jacket, and I was not disappointed. Here are the features I wanted and how well they satisfied my needs:WHAT I WANTEDI live near the ocean where mist, spray, and rain are playing all the time. Also, I’m planning a trip near the Rhine River where I expect it to be raining almost constantly. I wanted a light, combination windbreaker and rain jacket that I could pack in little space and rely on to keep me dry.WEIGHTMy Columbia Men’s Watertight II jacket weighs 15 ounces on my digital scale. That’s fine.WATERPROOFINGMy Columbia jacket has been out in some heavy rains, without any leaks. The sealed seams kept out the weather, the hood and cuffs didn’t leak, and I stayed dry.THE HOODThe nylon hood is large, and better worn over a cap. It adjusts with an elastic cord held tight in rubber washers. It keeps the wind away and blocks the rain well. If you pull the cord tight, it closes up the area under your chin.THE ZIPPERThe fine zipper keeps the jacket closed up and over your chin. Small patches of Velcro on the storm flap protect from sideways-blowing wind and rain. An elastic cord in a tensioner keeps the bottom loose or tight around your body.As in all other light jackets I have owned, you have to guide the zipper over folds in the fabric. If you grab it at the bottom and give it a John Wayne heave, it will get caught.THE SLEEVESThe sleeves are plenty long and close with Velcro bands, so wind and rain don’t sneak in. The sleeves are lined right down to the cuffs, with netting and a double layer of nylon. Whatever your arm length, the Velcro bands will keep the cuffs where you want them.THE POCKETSThere are two large mesh-lined side pockets with zippers under flaps. One of them has a double zipper so you can stuff the jacket inside the mesh pocket, leaving a zipper pull outside.BREATHABILITYOn windy days, the jacket keeps me warm, especially with a sweater underneath. I haven’t found myself perspiring as in nonbreathable fabric jackets. The coated nylon fabric is backed by an open mesh. When you move your arms and torso, air trapped inside the jacket vents, improving ventilation. If you want more ventilation, unzip the mesh pockets, and open the bottom.WINDPROOFINGWith the hood, sleeves, and bottom shut, the wind cannot leak inside. Several times on windy days, I thought it was calm and opened the zipper only to find the wind whipping through.RECOMMENDATIONSThis Columbia Men’s Watertight II jacket meets my requirements, and I look forward to wearing it around town and carrying it on my rainy trip. If what I’ve written appeals to you, you’ll like it too.

Title: Sizing is accurate

I typically wear a large size in a women's top and this jacket fit perfectly if I did not intend to wear a sweatshirt underneath. If I were to wear a sweatshirt underneath it would likely be too tight in the  lower abdomen and hip areas so I would size up. The arms give plenty of room without looking too big. The length is longer in back which is ideal for a wind jacket. I am 5ft 8" tall and wear a size 14 in jeans. If my hips were wider I would need an XL-- my hips measure 47 inches. Because this is a gift I won't be able to provide much feedback on wind or water resistance but can update later on.So in summary for my purposes (moderate build and chest size) I would say sizing was quite accurate and if one does not plan to layer anything bulky underneath then I would order your normal size.

Title: Light Weight Poncho Style Jacket - Stows In Built-In Pouch?
Review: Overall, I'm happy with this purchase.The sizing is spot on. The material looks durable. The zippers look to be good quality. It fits over my vest-style puffer jacket for layered insulation.The included pouch - sewn into the area over your stomach and into the same piece where you can put your hands inside - is a nice idea to protect something lightweight from the elements. Maybe even a cell phone.I didn't pay attention when ordering but was happy when I read that the jacket could be stowed within its built-in pouch. See photos. Well, I may not be the smartest person around, but... So: this pouch is completely sewn in all the way around. Pull it out as instructed and you have yourself a piece of mesh fabric that is stitched on all sides with no way in. There's even a zipper fob on the inside. Clearly the intent is to be able to access this, now inverted (as instructed), pouch. There's no way in from the other side if you flip the jacket inside out. If you stuff the lining of the pouch back in where it came from, sure you can stuff the jacket into this opening. But why? It makes a mess. It can't be zipped up. I'm better off just folding and rolling it and then stowing it in my pack or suitcase.This does not detract from the product. But, it leaves me scratching my head. Is there some online forum for "am I the idiot?" I might need to apply. Or, maybe, something got lost in translation somewhere.

I find these to be a good value and durable.  Before the COVID19 pandemic and having to stay home to isolate, I'd always wear these out.  With that much use a pair would last 2-3 years before the fabric would wear out.  Thanks to the pandemic, these pairs of jeans that I bought in 2019 still look new when I look closely at the fabric.  The pockets are also large (be careful when standing after sitting as some objects can fall out), and there are more than enough pockets for me, the standard 4 pockets plus additional pockets around the knee area.  If you're the kind of person I am, who doesn't like feeling restricted by clothing, then these are worth a try.

Title: Not the same as the Lee jeans that I've been buying for many, many years.
Review: Not the same as the Lee jeans that I've been buying for many, many years. I order a pair in January and the first time I wore them they fit great. Very relaxed as they should be. Then that afternoon I felt a draft on the back of my leg. I reached down only to find a tear in them. When I got home and put on an older pair. When I examined them, there was about a 1 inch by 1 inch right angle tear in them. After further tear examining them, there was another small tear next to the top of the rear pocket. I contacted Amazon and they replaced them right away.I started wearing the replacement pair. This was around mid February. Around 6 weeks ago, one of the bottom part of a belt loops tore off. Yesterday when I put these newest pair on I noticed the bottom part of another loops tore off. Examining them further, there are small tears next to the top of both rear pockets.Back in the day when I was working I used to buy anywhere from 4 and up to 12 pair of Lee jeans a year according to what kind of work I was doing. Now that I’m retired, I buy a new pair of jeans around once a year. I usually I have 1 new pair and around 4 to 5 old pairs to rotate. I’ve always mark the date that I bought them on the inside tags. So I know the older ones from the newer ones.  In the past 5 months, I only wore these jeans, maybe 25 to 30 days.Maybe I happened to get 2 defected pairs. I will buy one more pair and put them into rotation. If I have a problem again, I will have to try another brand.

Title: Awesome Jeans
Review: Jeans are somewhat personal, so what works for me may not work for you but I love these. I had 181s that I bought at the Lucky store and the combination of losing weight and starting to wear out wanted to get replacements. I checked the Lucky site first and they were no longer offered there. Some reason checked here on Amazon and they had them, Lucky Me! So I've been buying these (ok more like mini-hoarding them) on Amazon to solidify my jeans collection. I have both 32"x30" and 30"x30" and will likely order a pair of 31". Why? Sometimes need to tuck certain shirts in but also have times wear with t-shirt so not tucked, and by having multiple sizes I avoid either painful constriction or my pants falling down. My original Lucky jeans from 10+ years ago still kicking and I find that the sizing and fit is consistent. I'm slim/athletic but don't like the skinny cuts and also don't want to be too baggy so I find these are a happy medium. Not sure I would blindly order jeans online but happy that they are offered here. The Lucky You always makes me laugh. I do have Levis, but find that the sizing is not consistent and have to try on many different pairs before I find one that fits, and even then not sure how they are going to turn out until after the first wash.

Title: Great for a work-from-home dad who’s too tired to be cool.

I’m super lucky to get to live this way, but it always means changing my clothes if I want to run out to grab coffee, take my daughter to the park on my lunch break, or whatever. No biggie, but my days are long and sometimes that little annoyance is enough to dissuade me from getting out. These pants are comfy as hell and look like jeans, so I can rock them all day and still run an errand here or there without sacrificing the comfort I’ve been spoiled by or feeling like a bag of crap in line at Dunks.I’m a lifelong football and rugby player with thicc thighs and a rap video butt from years of pushing a sled and these things are loose and comfortable on me—which I LOVE, but my homies with leaner legs will want to take that into account when choosing a size. Thigh fit is usually the limiting factor for me when shopping for pants, so these being loose around the thighs means they’re probably bigger than you might expect.I’ve had these pants for a few weeks now and have no complaints whatsoever. Very comfortable, seem to be pretty good quality to me, and successfully maintains the illusion that I have enough self respect to get dressed in the morning. The inconspicuous elastic waist and draw string (hidden on the inside of the pants) also do wonders for my comfort level as I eat my anxieties about being the kind of guy who wears sweat pant jeans outside of my house totally non-ironically.These pants are worth their weight in broken fitness promises to myself. Good purchase.

Title: Oldschool Jeans, the way god intended
Review: Alright, so I usually don't write reviews, which is ironically what every scam reviewer writes haha!Anyhow, I saw the reviews here, and honestly I can't entirely speak of the sturdiness yet. I have bought three pairs of these jeans in 28x30.So far so good, I have recently started buying deadstock and vintage LEVIS 501 from pre-2000, which are much better quality than new LEVIS, unfortunately, both in fit and quality. In quality level I'll compare NEW-LEVIS, OG-LEVIS and the Wranglers bought here.1: QualityOG LEVIS, wins hands down, the quality of material and stitching is just streets ahead.However insofar as NEW-501 vs Wrangler  Authentic 5-pocket- Wrangler wins, as much as I like 501s, their quality ranges widely depending on production year and colour. Generally blue 501 have a good quality, but their other colours often come out stiff, for comparison I bought the Khaki in LEVIS 501, I believe they were called timberwolf colour, but the same as Khaki here. Incredibly stiff in the material, even after several washes. Whereas the Wrangler has been nice and soft even after a couple of test-washes!2: Sizing & FitOG Levis and the Wranglers here are quite similar in fit on the hip and in inseam. I usually use 30 inseam, but that often comes out too short on many pants, however vintage pants and jeans with inseam 30 fit me like a glove. With these wranglers out of the three pairs of jeans, the inseam has remained the same.New LEVIS terrible inseam, too short compared to description, I know that it is the fashion currently to have a pants-leg that is at ankle/above ankle length, which is fine, but unfortunately sellers sell with the inseam being 30, when in fact it is only 29 or so.NEW LEVIS have terrible fit on the hip as well, it is slightly below mid-rise I'd argue, and perhaps some of them barely above low-rise, so much inconsistency with the 501 currently.OG LEVIS, nice solid mid-rise waist-line, and I can say the same for these Wranglers.Insofar as the hip is concerned, a bit tight, same with OG LEVIS and NEW LEVIS; which I don't mind, this is the standard fit, not the relaxed or flex version.For all of the jeans. The thigh and calf fit is also nice and roomy if you buy in your size; I certainly don't have skinny legs, relatively muscular throughout and they are not too tight, a little strain on the thigh perhaps, and on the peak of the calf, but not uncomfortable.What started my jeans journey was actually waist/leg fit, rather than quality. I went to a local store and tried a pair of jeans on in 28x30, and I couldn't get them over my calf, and the tightness in the thigh was ridiculous not to mention how low they sat on my waist. When I checked the fit it wrote "Standard" after that it was a long journey to find that Wranglers are generally consistent and high quality especially considering the price.Wrangler used to have this 5-pocket as made in USA, I was lucky enough to buy a pair a couple of years ago, and unsurprisingly the material is nicer than what we currently have as well as construction of stitching, with that said this current version, imo has a better hip/waist fit, if just barely.I'll probably buy another 1-2 pairs of these at some point

I checked the PC9 code (found on the laundry instructions label), and the Levi's website says that what I got is "Dark Wash." So, it could be that Amazon simply shipped the wrong thing; maybe the photo *is* correct? I won't know until I get the replacements I requested.Update, a week later: Amazon sent my replacements, and they're exactly the same as the first shipment. I did *not* receive "Sequoia." The PC9 code on these is 18181-0027. I've tried to reach Amazon service to explain their problem to them, but there's no easy way these days to reach a human who might understand. So, again, if you like "Dark Wash," go ahead and order. There's nothing inherently wrong with the jeans, they're just not the "Sequoia" color shown on the web page.

Drying shrinks them up again and then they have to stretch out to fit.  They sit right on my hips at the belly button. The only thing I don't like is that I HAVE to wear a belt because they also stretch at the waist and me with a tummy and no waistline there is nothing to hold them up so they are always rolling over or sliding down.  This is a "me" problem, though I wonder if they could make the waistline not so stretchy.  Anyway I will keep buying until they don't make them anymore or I find something better but I have been looking for 15 years and these are still my fav.

Title: There are lines on my jeans
Review: I've worn Wrangler jeans for years and this pair I just received didn't disappoint for fit or style. However, what's up with the lines? Apparently, some colors have lines dyed into them. When I looked at the picture online I just thought they were creases in the jeans from wear; didn't pay much attention. But they are made and dyed to look as though they're old and creased or something, I'm not exactly sure. I've never owned jeans that naturally faded with lines across the front of them like that so I'm not sure what the look is that they're trying to achieve.But what the heck, these are supposed to be authentic and some of the colorways have lines and some don't. I just want regular old comfortable Wrangler jeans. I'll wear them out in my own way, thank you very much. It's too much trouble to return them so I'll live with the lines, but I'll be more careful next time I order jeans to make sure the manufacturers haven't dyed lines across them. This is as bad as the jeans that have holes in the knees. I used to patch them or cut them off when they developed holes in the knees but now people buy them that way and want them "pre-holed." What a world, what a world.

Title: Great. Though, not like first pair
Review: Just before pandemic closures bought a pair of these exact Wrangler’s at Theissen’s. My inseam is 35” which makes these a wee bit long. My other pair got tethered at the bottom of one leg. They’re my favorite so looked on Amazon rather then head to the store.Boom. There they were AND on sale. In the cart and in less then 24 hours on my door step.Immediately tried them on. Definitely keepers.A few differences I noticed. The pair from 2019 are my favorite jeans. But didn’t get worn a lot due to closures. But they were worn enough to have a lived in vibe. They’ve been washed a variety of times which adds to this comfortable feeling. This might be why they feel different.The original pair are super soft and the material is flexible in that unlike traditional stiff thick denim. They are thinner and feel like soft cotton sheets freshly laundered.The new pair material feels more like traditional denim. Not as thick. Not as soft. Washing may change this.This pair has stitching that is similar but more prominent thread. More noticeable. This also could be a wash and west difference.Overall side by side they’re almost identical. On, the newer doesn’t feel as flexible in the material. With some wearing this may change. They may get more soft over time.The new ones look great. Fit perfectly. Perfect length. Same pocket stitch on the back pockets.I’m really happy I found these. For the $33 yet 24 hrs later price tag of $37 wish I would have bought a second pair. In store a few years ago they were slightly more. The regular price of $42 is store retail I recollect.Overall, other then a few variations am super happy with this purchase. Especially now that the tethered heel is renewed by having a new pair.If you’re looking for a pair of jeans that will not be stiff and work with your figure if you lose or gain these May be your win.I was at the bottom of my weight class and my doctor asked me to gain weight concerned I was too thin. The paints worked with this change.I’ve decided to lose a few because ten was too much. These pants don’t require a new pair. They flex to fit. For me at least.If Wrangler continues to make these I’ll keep buying.⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️💯

Title: It’s a hit or miss with these jeans!
Review: I’m going to try to make this review as short as possible. Before ordering all 5 jeans (pictures 1-3) from this same page, I ordered one pair first to make sure the jeans fit. The jeans I ordered first are the darker jeans on picture #1.PICTURE #1 - In the first photo you’ll see two denim jeans, one light denim and one dark denim. Notice how both jeans have different tags on them: the light denim has a purple tag whereas the dark denim has a white tag. The white tag says, “AMANDA THE ORIGINAL SLIMMING JEAN” while the purple tag says, “AMANDA THE ORIGINAL DESIGNER JEAN”. So we can clearly see that they are NOT the same style jeans. Again, the dark denim jean fit me perfectly!PICTURE #2 - I ordered these other jeans, along with the light denim jean in picture 1, after trying on the the first pair. None of the jeans fit and they are all the size. The only difference is that some are Regular instead of Long but that shouldn’t matter because that has to do with the length. If one size 14 fits, all size 14s should fit.PICTURE #3 - this is another dark denim jean that I ordered. This is a different jean from the dark denim jean in picture 1. This jean is size 14 long just like the dark jean on picture 1 and it also fits perfectly!PICTURE #4 - all of the jeans (light denim, dark denim, black) are the same style; the light denim is size 14 Regular (this one doesn’t fit); the black jeans and the dark denim jeans are both 14 long, the SAME SIZE but the black one doesn’t fit whereas the dark denim does fit.Just keep that in mind when ordering. Not all size 14s will fit the same and you will not receive the exact same jeans. I received two different kinds: the  “AMANDA THE ORIGINAL SLIMMING JEAN” and the “AMANDA THE ORIGINAL DESIGNER JEAN”.NOT THE SAME JEANS!So remember, you can order 5 pairs of jeans the same size but most likely all of them won’t fit the same!I hope this review makes sense!!!!

Title: The fabric content is not as advertised.
Review: I ordered the Levi’s Women’s 721 High Rise Skinny Jean in Azure Mood, size 26 regular (= size 2, 30” long),  BECAUSE is it is advertised as 92% cotton and only 6% Poly and 2% Elastic.  I wanted the higher cotton content, and less stretch.  I knew as soon as I opened the package that these WERE NOT 92% cotton.  Waaay too much stretch to the fabric, and I wanted more “jean,” less “legging.”  These jeans, made in Sri Lanka consist of 71% Cotton (not 92%), 26% Viscose, 6% polyester, and 2% Elastine.  These jeans were oddly  tighter in the waist than the 720s I tried, and had far too much stretch otherwise…no control, no shaping.  Since Levi’s sold out, and stopped manufacturing all of their jeans in the USA, the manufacturer has lost its ability for reliable quality control or to uphold the traditional LEVI reputation.  Of course, there are Levi’s  jeans still made in the USA, but they aren’t affordable for most people looking for a well made, durable, but stylish pair of jeans.

Title: Love love love!!
Review: I used to only wear Levi’s when I was in my 20’s. Then I had a baby and I’m not sure if they made the high rise jeans yet but I stopped buying them. Now I’m 44 and I’m a Levi girl again! High rise all the way only because I get a muffin waist with anything else. These eliminated that for me completely. No more tight belts or having to constantly pull the waist of my jeans up. These are red tab Levi’s so the jean material is sturdier than the lesser priced one, which I tried before. Usually my jeans eventually rip in the upper inner thigh/crotch area. But not these!! I have several pairs and even my oldest pair is still going strong. They have a stretch to them that is a miracle for me. I work 12 hour shifts and always wear Levi’s. They are extremly comfortable.I live in Arizona so during the summer I wear the ones that have at least one rip in the legs which is like air conditioning for my legs. It is nice to grab a pair of jeans from my closet and always be putting on my favorite go-to jeans. I wash them inside out (unless I got something on them) and dry on medium and remove them from dryer before they are super hot.I wonder if I can buy stock in these because I believe these are the best jeans out there. I haven’t tried expensive jeans but expensive jeans start off with that negative of costing so much so I just don’t go there, it just doesn’t seem worth it to me. Even the highest priced Levi’s are a great buy. They have been doing jeans for a long time and they know how to make us look good.Keep in mind there are different #s for different fits so what ever you prefer for your body size and shape they will have something for you to love too!

Title: These looked more like the "rib cage" style on me.
Review: I'm 5'5 114lbs. I got them in 28 short, cause in the past "regular" Levi's jeans have always been obnoxiously long on me and I was curious if they would be better without all the excess length. Anyways, I actually DID like the "short" length (they were ankle length), but I didn't really like the rest of the style.These fit my 27 inch waist comfortably (they're high rise so they went above my belly button). The rest of the fit was too large for me though. While they did fit slightly slimmer in the butt and thighs they were a little baggy in the crotch and seemed to flare out a lot more than I expected (it was almost like a slimmer wide leg).They looked a lot more like the "rib cage" style Levis than "straight" on me, but maybe this is just because of my body shape (i have slim legs, so maybe they'd fit me more like a "straight" leg in a smaller size?) or maybe it's just the fact that i got them "short"? I don't know, but they don't look so flared in other reviewer's pictures, so it could be either of those things. FWIW, i did like the fabric and I can see how other people might like this style, but i just wanted boring straight leg jeans.

Title: I like it
Review: I need black pants for work, and frankly, since COVID I haven't worn anything except very forgiving soft pants. I like these because there's a small amount of stretch. I also like the matte black color. For jeans, the material is a little thin, but probably due to the stretch element. I am 5'4" but I never thought of myself as short. News Flash I AM short, lalala. I used "try before you buy" option, and I didn't even have to open the "regular" length version because the short version was below my ankle. There wasn't much difference between a size 12 or 14, but I chose to stick with the larger size in case they shrink in the wash. If you are optimist chose the smaller size, if you are pragmatic pick the larger. The smaller size will fit because the stretch has a little give. The larger size will fit me without any stretch at all, so if you like feeling held into place, go smaller. If you like a loose (it won't really be loose like relaxed jeans) but if you want the old fashioned feeling of jeans with no stretch size up.

They arrived the day after I ordered them, I tried them immediately, and was about to take them to the UPS store when I decided to wait till the next morning. I found a return label in the bag and took it the next morning after 9AM. Then Saturday evening I see an Email I have a charge of $38.22 made at two something in the morning Eastern time. I thought I was hacked!!! I call Amazon’s number on my Chase Amazon card. On the third try I got a good connection. The first two were static and muffled. Not a good thing for conveying info. This poor soul could not help because of the hour of the day, most other dept were closed. He kindly offered to call me later when I would be able to talk with the dept. I needed. I said no because everyone in my house would be asleep. That was the end of my conversations with Amazon.  So my take on Try Before You Buy? FORGET ABOUT IT! Title: Nice
Review: Size 8. 5'6" 155lb, (being modest) I have a tiny waist, broad hips, moderate butt. I carry my weight in muscular upper body, and dense lower body these days.I usually wear pretty curvy jeans, because the waste usually gaps in EVERYTHING I own. I wear a belt with ALL my jeans, because of the gap.These jeans fit well, enough that I might consider a size 6 next, with the expectation of a tighter fit. Not perfect fit in the waist, but they probably are a decent "curvy" fit. I liked Levi 529, this is a close next best.  I wear a belt so I dont have to keep hiking jeans up, but find I did pull these up several times a day.The legs are mostly straight through the thigh, a tiny bit narrower at the knee, but not much taper after that. I have solid thighs, and large calves (boot buying is never fun) and own slim ankles... these jeans do not cling, but wearing a neoprene knee brace underneath leaves no spare room. I might have considered a 6, but was hoping for space for the brace.The fabric feels like traditional modern denim, not 1920s canvas-denim, and not leggings style stretch-denim...., just modern denim with a tiny bit of stretch... which I hoped meant 2-3 days wear, without looking /feeling worn out.  But they just seem to relax over the first day, and bummer, feel like "5th day wear" on the second day... so to me, that's 1 day wear jeans.Color was good.

Review: I tugged at the waistband, then pulled these on without even unbuttoning or zipping! That's how stretchy these pants are at the top. Too weird. I even ordered a sized down. They probably shouldn't have even fit at all. They weren't huge, but I wanted them to fit better in places for my aging body - lol. I wanted the fabric to consist of mostly cotton. I mean, they're Levi's, right? I didn't want leggings type fabric. The style is very good, not skinny, not wide, or boot-cut. Very straight like 90s jeans. The fabric is far more substantial than, say, ON jeans.  Also, the description states the size Short pants should be 27/30, but they are actually labeled 27/28 size 4 in reality. Disappointing. Will be sizing down *again* and ordering 26 Regular, hoping the length will be 30" as I've seen in another review. Will probably update later.Update: Received replacement and they were imperfect, some kind of stain or something on the leg. Pants are so incredibly stretchy, not really what I expected in Levi's at all. Not the quality I was expecting. Also, even the smallest size available 26 (2) reg could probably fit size 6. They seem ok for around the house I guess. Not wide legged, similar to slim straight 90s jeans. Short is 28", Regular length is 30". Rise is a little bit higher on me than mid rise.Final decision:  I think these are too stretchy and have such a low cotton content, they don't really feel like Levi's, more like Levi's Signature jeans. They're really just too stretchy and loose in the lower stomach that they're not flattering there. I expected better from Levi's.

Review: I imagine that everyone struggles with finding jeans that fit their body perfectly and you are probably familiar with the struggle of trying on every different brand you can find before finding one that works for you and for me that is Levis. So I went to Kohl's in search of Levi's capris and found these. They have the perfect amount of stretch and fit me beautifully in my normal size 16 but I only purchased one pair because they were $70! Then I came home and got on Amazon to find another pair. I found these at half the price in the color that I purchased; unfortunately, when I tried them on I had the same problem as other reviewers, even though I purchased the same size, which here is 33, they were too big. I have had the same issue with Levi's before and I don't know if it is because they are made in Sri Lanka or not but it's a big problem. Obviously, this is not Amazon's fault and in fact, Amazon makes things very easy with their return policy. So I set up a return and decided to order a size 32 and another size 33 to hopefully get one that fit properly. I also discovered Amazons try it before you buy it which made things even easier. So when my package arrived, I first tried on the size that should fit me and thankfully, they did so I did not even have to open the plastic bag on the other pair of pants. And setting up this return was just as easy. All I had to do was go on the app and choose what I was keeping and follow the directions for returning the ones I did not want. The size issue is the reason for for 4 stars, but I do recommend these jeans but you may want to order a couple of different sizes under the try it first program and hopefully you will end up with a pair that fits the first time around and returns are very easy. Simply follow the instructions and return The Unwanted merchandise to your nearest UPS store

Title: Quality As Expected From Levi's, But A Bit of Sizing Issue
Review: Pros- solid quality I expect from Levi's, 99 percent cotton. Now with that in mind, I haven't worn 501s since the 90s, and most jeans these days have a lot of stretch and when I shop, I take that into account when buying a pair of jeans online. In  the Levi Strauss & Co. Gold Label Women's Curvy Totally Shaping Straight Jeans which I purchase on here, I wear an 8 which is a 30 waist, they are also like 60 percent synthetic. Amazon suggested a 32 for me. It was Prime Day and it was a lightening deal at such a good price, my dumb self didn't look at the percentage of cotton or I would have gone up a size from suggested as these are definitely tight in the waist on me. As for me I am apple shaped, all my weight is in my gut. If I was hourglass or pear, I do think the suggested size would be fine.Also, I got the short length. I am barely 4'11 and I am always happy when brands offer short. They hit right at my ankle. The crotch is an eensy bit long, but that's the life of a short person.  I expected this and am satisfied.I would normally would have exchanged these, but alas I am out of town so I am going to keep then and down what I did back in day--lay down on the floor to button them up and wear them around the house to stretch them out. I'll definitely be air drying these babies, but I am also going to get a new pair in the proper waist and run those through the dryer and enjoy the old school denim feel, something that I did't realize I missed. If you haven't worn jeans that are 100 or 99 percent cotton, you're in for a treat. They really do get better with age and you don't have to worry about butt sag. They also are warmer in the winter and cooler in the summer.

Title: Buy your normal size!
Review: Okay so I did some research on the Levi 501's. They are supposed to fit tight at first and then you break them in. So buy your normal size. Unless you want a boyfriend fit, then buy a size up. In my research you need to break them in and they can loosen up to an inch to an inch and a half. To do this, wear them around the house for a day or two and do a lot of stretching and squats. If you dont want to break them in over time, get in the shower with them and let the warm water on them. Then get out and wear them till they dry.. its insane, but this is a thing! The rigid style is super flattering and once they are broken in they are the most comfortable things ever and will last a long time! Don't wash in the machine often! Every 10 wears will do.

They have way more stretch to them, way less “denim.” Wedgies fromNordstrom are much more stiff and less stretch, which is what I like since they have less spandex and more denim. That said, I think these are authentic, but lower line Levi’s, which makes sense given the cheaper price. This price is the same as the outlet price. Title: Not the same as the Lee jeans that I've been buying for many, many years.
Review: Not the same as the Lee jeans that I've been buying for many, many years. I order a pair in January and the first time I wore them they fit great. Very relaxed as they should be. Then that afternoon I felt a draft on the back of my leg. I reached down only to find a tear in them. When I got home and put on an older pair. When I examined them, there was about a 1 inch by 1 inch right angle tear in them. After further tear examining them, there was another small tear next to the top of the rear pocket. I contacted Amazon and they replaced them right away.I started wearing the replacement pair. This was around mid February. Around 6 weeks ago, one of the bottom part of a belt loops tore off. Yesterday when I put these newest pair on I noticed the bottom part of another loops tore off. Examining them further, there are small tears next to the top of both rear pockets.Back in the day when I was working I used to buy anywhere from 4 and up to 12 pair of Lee jeans a year according to what kind of work I was doing. Now that I’m retired, I buy a new pair of jeans around once a year. I usually I have 1 new pair and around 4 to 5 old pairs to rotate. I’ve always mark the date that I bought them on the inside tags. So I know the older ones from the newer ones.  In the past 5 months, I only wore these jeans, maybe 25 to 30 days.Maybe I happened to get 2 defected pairs. I will buy one more pair and put them into rotation. If I have a problem again, I will have to try another brand.

I can still wear them with the belly and they'll be great without. If the rise bothers you, they'd still be comfortable rolls down one. Inseam is about 3-4", which I also like, because it keeps things covered, and shorts are narrow enough that you don't have to worry about them riding up easily.I ordered the one with the long sleeve/sweatshirt-like top and it is super comfortable too. It is a loose fitting top, just as the picture shows. I've only worn it a couple times due to being pregnant, but considering it fits over the belly now (albeit a bit short), it is going to be perfect afterwards. I have stronger arms and shoulders, and this fits across everything very comfortably. I will say that overall, it fits probably just SLIGHTLY larger than I would normally expect for a Medium (as someone who is typically a sz 6-8, athletic build) however since these are comfortable clothes, it isn't enough that I would size down at all. They're pretty perfect in my book!

There are easy ways to learn a lesson, and then are hard ways… with a day or two I had broken out in a bright red contact dermatitis rash all over my whole body except the head, hands & feet … the only place that the pajamas don’t touch, imagine that! Thickest around the forearms and wasteband line, where the pajamas are tightest against the skin… imagine that! It doesn’t itch, so maybe I should give 2 stars… unresponsive to Benadryl, unresponsive to steroid cream, no fever, no other symptoms, fully vaccinated for measles and already had the chicken pox as a child so… I wonder what gave me the rash, hmm… after 5 days it has not gone away. After I see the DOCTOR on Monday about this sudden *full body* rash, I will gladly update this review if the diagnosis is anything other than nasty-pajama-chemical-induced contact dermatitis. Title: The best pants ever made
Review: Title says it all. 5.11 tactical pants are durable, comfortable and (at least this style of them) have all the pockets you will ever need.The right side has a velcro pocket at the side of the knee that is perfect for a phone or a wallet. Right above that is a pen pocket. The left side has the velcro pocket at the knee great for a phone or wallet. Above that is another thinner velcro pocket about the right size for a flashlight. Then you have the standard right and left side pants pockets. Right behind the side pockets, facing towards the front, are the back pockets. These close in the middle with a strip of velcro and are perfect for a CCW.On the first belt loop to the right is a metal keyring.  And between the right side and back pocket is a hammer loop.The waist is elastic so the feel is roomy. The material is very sturdy. I have accidentally spilled water on it before and was surprised that the water beaded instead of soaking in. These are durable enough to be used as a pair of work pants but they look nice enough to be used as casual dress pants.

I've been using a Columbia rain jacket for a couple years now and it's a great, versatile, waterproof piece, so I'm sure these pants will be the same. I love that these also have the mesh lining for air flow and so you are not touching the waterproof coating of the shell fabric, which in my experience can irritate my skin, even through clothing. I'm glad I finally bought these nice rain pants and am sure they will come in handy for a long time, even as nice lightweight snow pants worn over warm leggings.

Title: Great rain pants

And, the biggest bonus is that they come in a short length which I was only able to find on Amazon (I'm 5'3"). I had tried the regular length which were way long on me. My son (who has the same pants) and I were comfortable the entire time we were outdoors.

Title: 400+ miles on a motorcycle in torrential rain and STILL dry!!!!!

Sewed an elastic to the bottom so that they don't rise up my boots, and I couldn't be happier with them. Seriously, 400+ miles on the worst of days and I was dry. I felt damp from sitting on a soaked seat, but, I was dry. I also like how they breath. There's not a sauna happening inside. Going to buy the matching jacket and toss out the Joe Rocket that leaves me feeling like I've gone swimming with all my clothing on. (I'm wearing a size Small in the pics)

Title: I wish I'd bought them years ago
Review: I have been desperate to find a fabric mosquitos can't bite through until it dawned on me: waterproof. But then finding pants that were ACTUALLY 100% waterproof was a whole other issue. THESE ARE. I've bathed the dogs while wearing them, they are completely waterproof and better than that, THEY'RE MOSQUITO PROOF. I get snacked on like a juice box once it's warm in Texas and typically they only EVER bite my legs (even though I never wear shorts and I'm always in a tank top) and that is where I have a weird horrible allergic reaction to them. Since I got these, I don't go outside without them on and now they're just biting me on the back like cowards (but i don't have an allergic reaction to those so whatever i guess) SO THE PANTS ARE DOING THEIR EXTRA JOB. Zero bites on my legs.As for fit, I got x-small, I'm about 5'4 and weigh 100 pounds and they fit perfect. I probably could have gotten the shorter fit and it would have been fine but I don't mind a little extra length at the bottom, they're not dragging on the ground or swallowing my feet or anything like that. They DON'T have pockets, however there is one small pouch on the inside that you could put something small in like a wallet or money (it wouldn't fit a phone its not that big).They do do the swish swish sound like windbreakers so if you're looking for quiet pants, these aren't them, but otherwise, they ARE waterproof and they are mosquito proof, and they're comfortable and light enough to wear in texas heat without feeling like theres a swamp in my pants.

Why can't manufacturers offer women's petite plus sizes that would have more adjustment in the waist and can be bought at the right length for those of us who are shorter "fluffy" ladies?  We like the outdoors and being active, too!  Sigh....I took my trip without the pants, managed to stay dry most of the time thankfully.

Title: COMFORTABLE!!
Review: I have to admit, I was a bit apprehensive when I bought these.I'm generally a jeans guy and have never bought stretch pants of any kind. I also didn't know what to expect from the fabric.POSITIVESI'm 65, and over the years have gained a few inches in the waist.  I was getting tired of cinching down my belt in order to keep my pants up without "saggy butt syndrome" or feeling like I was being choked to death at the waist when I sat down.So, ideally I wanted a pant that was lightweight, cool to wear in the heat, with lots of give in the waist, seat & inseam. I also was looking for a pair that did double-duty as a casual, everyday pair that was semi-dressy/business casual.Voila - these pants of hit on all cylinders.  I worked for 30 years in the IT industry where "business casual" was the standard dress code. These are an ideal replacement for the traditional "khakis".The best part of these, hands down is their COMFORT.  Typically when I was working, the first thing I did when I got home was to get out of my suit or business casual clothes and put on a well-worn pair of jeans.  These are WAY more comfortable than any pair of jeans.No that I'm retired, my typical "around-the-house" casual attire is a pair of jeans, pajama bottoms, or lounging pants.These Lees are so comfortable that I could see myself wearing them all day.Fabric - the fabric on these is different than anything I've ever worn.  Heavier than a nylon, lighter than a cotton.  To the touch the fabric has a bit of a velvety feel.NEGATIVESThe only real negative I can think of is that they seem to tend to pick up a little lint.  Not real bad, but just something my wife noticed.Bear in mind that I didn't wash them before I wore them the first time, so after first wash, this may change.The only other thing is that after being a jeans guy my whole life, I think it's going to take me a little time of wearing these before I feel like they will replace my jeans.

And it's not just a chemical smell; it is that, but somehow it also conjures a strong undertone of aged sewage and rotting rat.  They are fine otherwise (except the size/shape of the pockets is a little weird), and running them through the washer two or three times in a row cleared up the smell. Title: Great quality pants
Review: I love these pants - I originally bought them in the 'Carbon Rinse' color (worn once so far), just got the 'Navy/Gray Windowpane' (not worn out yet) and now need to have them in all the colors. This is a review for the 'Navy/Gray Windowpane' Lee Women's Flex Motion Regular Fit Trouser Pant in size 10 (regular, not long or short lengths). TLDR: Buy these pants.For reference I'm 5'5" and ~173 lbs, with an hourglass figure, measurements 41/31/43.Size/Fit: Both size 10s I've ordered are consistent with each other and true to size of a size 10, with a comfortable amount of stretch at the waistband – the fabric itself isn't super stretchy like workout pants or anything, but has a great blend to look polished and feel comfortable. At 5'5" the regular length will be great with a reasonable heel without any hemming. The 'regular' fit of the leg hangs nice and fairly straight from my hips (dips in slightly about mid-thigh) for a clean line. Pockets lay flat and smooth. Rise goes right to/maybe slightly under my navel.Look/Details: Pattern and color are exactly as shown on my screen – a nice rich navy with mid-tone gray lines throughout. Button closure is a nice-looking glossy navy with silver accent which makes the pants look fancier too, and the windowpane print lines up perfectly on the front/crotch and back/butt seams which makes the pants look higher quality as well.Comparing colors/fabrics: The 'Navy/Gray Windowpane' are a slightly different fabric/feel than the Carbon Rinse color (which is slightly thicker and barely stiffer and feels more like a polished, quality trouser jean) – both are great quality and are extremely comfortable.Seller: My 'Navy/Gray Windowpane' pair came from Smarter Solutions, arrived quickly and was packaged well. Would buy items from this seller again.

Title: Old school shirts in all the best ways!
Review: Carhartt shirts (and shorts) are my go-to for everyday wear. Excellent quality material and manufacture, a variety of styles and fabrics and colors, a nice "simple" look that's timeless. And mainly... Carhartt is one of the last manufacturers to make their clothes in true sizes.I have given handfuls of brand-name t-shirts to Goodwill because their "2XL" has shrunk so much it's two effective sizes smaller. They often fit through the chest and shoulders, but have gotten shorter and shorter over the years to the point where the hem barely meets my belt. Going to 3XL or even 4XL just makes them baggy and sometimes even then still too short.Carhartt is still a full size for each size, like some of my oldest treasured shirts. Worth the moderate extra cost, especially given their like-iron longevity!Gotta cop, though... I always cut the logo square off before a first wash. Partly because I don't wear brands on the outside (even ones I admire), but mostly because the darn little square is so stiff it will scratch you!

Title: Good thick fabric, 100% cotton NOT tagless but tag rips off easily
Review: As long as you’re not a delicate little flower.  Then these are fine shirts. Good thick fabric, 100% cotton (but low thread count feel), will shrink, NOT tagless but tag rips off easily.For this price point, there is no point in complaining as if you paid more so here are some things to expect:It’s 100% cotton so it’s going to shrink since it’s not “pre-shrunk”It’s possible these are “fake” as many claim, or it may be Hanes cutting back on quality control. There is no way to knowing one way or another but here are some observations.Got 3 packs and 1 shirt had a hole in the back already.Shirts will NOT arrive in Factory branded bags, they’ll be in generic sealed plastic bags (my guess is because its easier for “try before you buy returns” to be folded/packaged/resealed for the next buyer) so wash before wearing.This is NOT tagless, but the tag does tear off easily. This doesn’t PROVE these are fake of knock offs (Maybe Hanes has a large stockpile of tags they can sew on for the cost of nothing instead of spending on the special ink, running the machinery and employees trained to operate said machinery to get that tagless. Idk.These are most likely 100% cotton as claimed so they WILL shrink! I find the larger the shirt size the more they will shrink relative to their size. So plan accordingly.A common complaint is that they’re itchy. All I can say is WASH BEFORE WEARING as you should be anyways. Ever heard of demodex mites? Now you have.Another complaint is that they feel rough. this isn’t 3000 thread count Egyptian cotton feeling more like 300 thread count. With that said these are FAR thicker than the genuine Hanes shirts I’ve bought in store in the last few years. Personally, I’ve never noticed.Bottom line: If you are the type of guy who may not even own a pair of cargo pants (anymore) but loved them because of its functionality. Who knows what SAE/metric is, and doesn’t wear tight jeans (by choice).Chances are very high you’ll be happy with these.$2.50/shirt + tax

Title: No longer tagless!!!
Review: Have bought many of these over the years and they were indeed tagless. However, although the product description still claims "Tagless neck label for comfort" that is no longer true. Not only weren't they tagless but both shirts actually had 2 tags sewn into them. After searching the Q&A and Reviews for the word tag, it appears many others are similarly disappointed in this new development. Being tagless was always one of the key features of these shirts going back to when they were first introduced. Hanes made a big deal out of it... and rightfully so. It's so much nicer not having physical tags scraping and scratching your neck. Therefore, I'm extremely disappointed in them for a) allowing this change to perpetuate despite all the customer complaints and b) making no effort to get the product description corrected so it doesn't keep misleading customers. Until that happens, if you also don't like receiving tagged shirts that were promised to be "Tagless neck label for comfort" then I suggest you return them using the reason of Not As Described and also post a review here. Title: Nice jacket-shirt. I'm happy with the purchase.
Review: Overall, I'd say this jacket-shirt exceeded expectations. First impression is that it is more hefty than I expected, which is a good thing. For warmth, I would say that it's warm enough for fall/spring in my area (mid-Atlantic), especially if you put a good base layer under it. But it is not heavy enough for winter, which is fine. I bought this as a cool weather jacket and have heavier jackets for colder weather. Water does bead a bit on the outer fabric, but I'll probably wax it if/when that beading starts to go away.The "barley" color that I got matched the Amazon photos pretty well. At first glance (and in the Amazon photos), the shirt appears to have a rugged, worn-in look with a bit of natural color texture from "wear". But it's not color texture, the outer fabric actually has a bit of sheen that reflects light giving that effect. The fabric also has an unexpected feel: Instead of a slightly coarse cottony feel, it has a smooth satiny feel. And the cloth is very tightly woven - more so than your usual work shirt. None of this matters to me as I like both the look and feel of it. But if you're particular that a shirt like this should look and feel a certain way, then you may not like it. The inside is lined with cotton flannel for the torso and polyester for the sleeves. Lining the sleeves with a slicker cloth makes it easier take off without accidentally turning the sleeves inside-out, but if you prefer maximum insulation, polyester is not ideal.The sizing was pretty true to the chart. Maybe just a tad bigger, but not much. Be aware that it's not a modern slim fit though; it's a regular or classic fit. I'm 6'2" and 210 lbs and the LT size fit pretty ideally with the sleeve cuffs folded up, which is what I wanted. I recommend taking measurements of yourself to ensure you order the right size. A few minutes of effort before you order could avoid several days of delay and a lot of hassle after.

Title: Durable, Attractive, Multi-Functional Shirt/Jacket

I mentioned that I ordered several different colors and styles of this brand. Fortunately, the son who attends college in Boulder ended up with this one. All of the other Legendary Whitetails Shirt/Jackets I ordered were more on the shirt side of a shirt/jacket. This worked out well for us because we live in Louisiana, my other son is in Pharmacy school in the deep south, and my two nephews live in Texas.This Shirt/Jacket is exceptionally comfortable and is good for colder weather. It's not clothing you would want to keep on while inside.Regarding sizing, my son said it is true to size. He is a true Medium in nearly everything I purchase. He's 20 years old, 5'10 or maybe 5'll, and about 160 pounds. He works out and is fit, but has broad shoulders. I bought a size Medium for my husband as well. He is 170, 5'10. My other son is about the same height and weight.They can easily wear a shirt, sweatshirt, hoodie, or turtleneck beneath the shirt/jacket. I suggest ordering your normal size unless you like your jackets to fit baggy or you are larger in the stomach area. If you live in the north or midwest and plan on layering more than one article of clothing under the shirt/jacket, you may want to consider the bigger size.This shirt/jacket is a remarkable deal for the price. Everyone who received one as a gift from me has worn theirs multiple times. The jackets look better now -- with that worn-in look. It keeps the bitter cold of Michigan from biting and protects from harsh wind. The shirt/Jacket has several interior and exterior pockets.I can tell when someone genuinely likes a gift and this topped our family Christmas bestseller list and has already been added to the repeat performer list for 2022.If you're looking for a heavier shirt/jacket for colder months, one that you can layer or wear over a sweatshirt or hoodie, this is for you. If you are looking for a lighter-weight shirt/jacket that you can leave on indoors then I would try one of Legendary Whitetails many other shirt/jacket options.Overall, this is a fabulous product. It outperforms competitors in value, purpose, and appearance. That’s a winner in my opinion

I tend to like the pinks, yellows and coral colors but the colors are diverse and they hold up well.  Like any cotton product, they definitely will shrink in the dryer to a point but then they don't shrink.  I'm 5'9, 180 pounds and the medium is perfect for me after it shrinks.  Occasionally, I will stretch out the shirt just a little after it comes out of the dryer so its looser in the arms but that's similar with all polos with the stretch band in the bicep area.  At any rate, the shirts are tailored nicely and wear very well.  I continue to buy them and use them for work and weekends.  Excellent shirts.....

Title: Nice t-shirt depending upon what you're looking for.
Review: I bought 3 of these shirts in Dusk Blue, Dusty Green, and White.  I'm 6'0" tall with a 44" chest, 17" biceps, and a 34" waist.  I weigh about 207 lbs and have a muscular build with fairly low body fat.  I wasn't looking for a skin tight muscle shirt or compression shirt.  I just wanted a clean fitting t-shirt for summer that I can wear under a linen button up shirt without a bunch of baggy fabric at the waist.The reviews regarding size are all over the place.  I'll give you my take on sizing and fit along with overall construction and quality.  Spoiler alert, the sizing is a perfectly normal US standard.  A L is a L and an XL is an XL.So, most reviews stated that these shirts run small and recommend sizing up 1 or even 2 sizes.  I ordinarily take that with a grain of salt because most US guys are shopping a "slim fit" shirt like this despite the fact they are sporting 30% body fat and most of that sits around their waist.  People are delusional.But there were so many reviews recommending sizing up, I took the bait and ordered the 3 shirts in XL.  As I feared, the XL fit way too large.  The chest was not bad but not the snug fit I wanted.  The neck was OK.  And the sleeves were OK.  But the length was way too long.  And there was way too much extra fabric around the waist.  They looked sloppy on me.Guys, just because you're 6'0" tall and 207 lbs like me does NOT mean we are built the same.  I can only surmise that a lot of guys leaving these reviews have no upper body muscle mass or leg development and carry a lot of their weight around their belly.  The classic pear shape of a sunken chest, and spare tire, and chicken legs says you should be shopping foe a "classic fit" t-shirt, not a slim fit shirt with spandex.I sent the XL shirts back and ordered the same 3 colors in my usual size L.  The fit of the size L is perfect.  The neck is a high V.  The sleeves are snug against my biceps.  The chest is snug but not muscle shirt tight.  And there is enough of a taper towards the waist to keep it looking fitted and clean but again, not like a muscle shirt.  It looks casual and well fitted without being too baggy or so tight that it shows off everything under it.As for the fabric, I got what I expected.  I have some white dress t-shirts that are 95% cotton and 5% spandex and I figured these would be similar.  They are.  Adding spandex to cotton makes it stretchy but it also makes it weirdly smooth and adds a little bit of shine.  It ends up looking and feeling a little like polyester more than cotton. So if you expected that typical Hanes white t-shirt look with a matte finish, you may be disappointed.  On the other hand, the spandex keeps about 90% of the wrinkles out of the cotton shirt and makes it really comfortable to wear.  Again, the no wrinkle look is a little like polyester but is keeps looking sharp all day.As for construction, the neck is really well stitched.  Same with the sleeves and the waist.  The label is printed which I prefer rather than a tag.  Overall, this is the clean, slim fit look I was hoping for.In summary, this is a nice, slim fit shirt well suited for casual wear alone or under a long sleeve button up shirt worn unbuttoned in hot weather.  If you are muscular with low body fat just order your normal size.  If you are a typical US male with no muscle and a big belly, yeah, order up a size or two.  Or maybe look at some t-shirts that are "classic fit" without spandex to avoid drawing attention to your waistline.Hope this helps.

Review: Overall this is a great shirt. Though, not as great as the Calvin Kline version I can no longer find. I've bought several in different colors over the last year and as yet, have not had one come apart on me though I feel a few have shrunk.  I really like that they don't thread a plastic tag through the product and instead opt for a clip akin to a safety pin. There are several tags attached to this pin, they do not contain washing instructions despite having plenty of places to print that information. Printed on the inside of the shirt there are what appear to be washing symbols. I've had several young people try to explain these symbols to me but their expressive interpretive dances have failed to successfully communicate the proper instructions. On the upside, they seem to like to touch the shirt and while doing so they give way to soft cooing and purring noises that soon have fingers pulling and tugging to remove all clothing. Though I've had no complaints personally, I would very much like these shirts to be thicker and I would pay more for a thicker version. In the meantime, I've emailed the archeological department of the local university in hopes of bringing these symbols to an egyptologist who caught my fancy when I stumbled into their lecture by accident. My hope is that their knowledge of ancient hieroglyphics can shed some light on the symbols of my shirt and I would be interested to know if these shirts are as soft as Egyptian cotton. Title: quality product
Review: Purchased three shirts to compare.. The green shirt appears to be made with predyed yarn, had very little downstretch and about 100 pct width stretch. The finished chest width was about 45" around. This is the most representative of a T Shirt in my opinion.  A good 28 cut 40 singles combed yarn mercerized  fabric without spandex would make a perfect t shirt. The Spandex brings up the cost and creates a bit of inconsistency.The orange and black shirt had lots of width and downstretch, too much in my opinion. The fabric was a bit thick for a t-shirt.  As a result the cost for the fabric is excessive and more shirt than required or needed.The black shirt is basically the same as the orange shirt.Since I was buying a t-shirt, the least expensive (green) would be more acceptable to most.All in all the quality is good, but all are different. Hard to buy from Amazon when you're not sure what you will receive. If I buy six T Shirts it would be better if all of the fabrics are about the same. Nevertheless all three are quality shirts, but if you buy 4 or 5 colors, you won't know what you will get.

Title: Medium is gargantuan but maybe they'll shrink too
Review: I'd previously ordered a medium in Navy (May 2021) and the fit was what I'd call "relaxed." I kept them because, though I like long pants more fitted, a pair of loose shorts is perfect for lounging around the house, gardening, or exercise (a kind of "full" fit that allows completely unrestricted movement).  Back then, I used the Amazon recommendation to determine my size selection. (It was based on purchases of size 4 32" inseam Wrangler jeans and Baleaf highwaisted size S 32" length yoga pants and Prana size 2 reg Halle hiking pants among other orders.) In other words, I bought what I "knew" was one size too big, because I wanted exactly that "full" fit. (My stats are: 5'8", 130 lbs, waist 26", hips 36.5".)This most recent pair is Light Steel. Right out of the package, the fit on them is beyond loose. I am hoping they'll shrink, because they are NOT at all flattering -- too long (touching my kneecaps!) and tent-like in the waist and hips. I'd swear they didn't have a size chart when I ordered my Navy pair and a look at the current chart would suggest a size XS. Besides after laundering the Navy ones, they were the right amount of loose for me.Here's the current (Aug 2022) chart:US WOMEN'S SHORTS SIZE CHARTSize  Waist  HipXS  27 - 28  35.5 - 36.5S 28.5 - 29.5 37.5 - 38.5M 30.5 - 31.5 39.5 - 40.5L 33 - 34.5 42 - 43.5XL 36.5 - 39 45.5 - 47.5XXL 41 - 43.5 49.5 - 51.53XL 45.5 - 48 53.5 - 55.5I also have a Black pair (size M) ordered, but they're not due to arrive for another 5 days. My history with Hanes is that there can be HUGE differences in fit and fabric content between colors, so I will give the Black ones a chance. Title: Size down! ...and be prepared to wear a belt.
Review: These shorts are comfortable and seem like they fit good when you initially try them on, but by the time you start walking around, they become very loose. I've had to size down twice, and thinking about going down to the next size.I initially ordered my normal size 9 but found myself pulling them up most of the day. I ordered a size 7 and though they seemed slightly tighter, was still uncomfortably loose within an hour or so of wearing them.I recently received the size 5 that I ordered but they were noticeably loose, pulling on without even having to unbutton them. This prompted me to compare the sizes.As you can tell in the pictures, the size 7 is much smaller than the size 5. I even borrowed my friend's size 5 to compare a washed and new pair. I thought, maybe they shrink after wash, but that doesn't seem like the case here.Side note: After speaking to my friend who owns the same shorts, she is experiencing the same issues with the sizes. She has sized down 3 times and considering trying the next size down. It almost seems impossible to get the right fit here. Something, possibly the stretch of the waist seem, is very off. I feel like I need those waist adjusters found in children's clothes here.So what you should know is that:1) these shorts are very stretchy2) you should definitely size down3) the color will fade just a bit after wash4) and just because you order a specific size, it's highly possible that they won't fit like that size should.Even though I've struggled in finding a good fit with these shorts, I'll still give them 4 stars because everything else about them is great. They are a good length, big pockets, and comfortable everywhere except the waist.

Title: My favorite shorts ever!
Review: I wore Levi's Bermuda shorts for years. I'm a curvy gal (5' 4", 185 lbs) and as I aged I just felt more comfortable in longer shorts. But I finally decided I was tired of that look and wanted to get something shorter--but not short-short. I decided to try these since they were labeled "mid" length. On me, with chonky thighs, they were a little too short for my comfort as they came. But for all the people in other reviews who say they can't be unrolled--of course they can be! The cuffs are secured in place by one stitch on the inside of the thigh and one on the outside. It's a simple matter of snipping that stitch on each side and voila...you've just given yourself an extra inch or or two in length by unrolling the cuffs. Unrolled, they're perfect for me! I've bought four pairs of these now, in different colors/shades, and I've been able to snip the stitch and unroll all of them with ease. It doesn't affect the side seams in the shorts at all.These are now my favorite shorts ever!! Be aware, though, that as with most Levi jeans/shorts, different colors are sometimes made in different places and the sizing isn't always consistent.  I typically wear a size 12 in most pants. I have two pairs of these shorts in size 31 (size 12) and two pairs that fit better in size 32 (14), so you may have to play around a bit to find the right fit for you based on the color you pick. In general, though, they're more or less true to size.

The size is just right, and if I do reduce in size--which I hope to do--there is a drawstring at the top so I can always tighten that. Also, they have really nice zippered pockets which is great for carrying small objects like lip balm or tissue. I am sweaty when I get home, and all I do is swish these in some water with a dash of vinegar and let them dry flat under a ceiling fan. This way I don't have to run them through the washing machine every time. They dry really fast. Very happy with this purchase. :)

Title: If you are into moist & sweaty balls, hit the buy now button!
Review: Who can't pass up a deal, right? At $15 I thought I was getting a great deal...I mean compared to the name brand, made in USA that I pay $40+ for. Well as we all know you get what you pay for and Amazon is here to keep reminding us that. First, construction is great! Material choice, well lets just say, they inner short, spandex like material does an excellent job at retaining moisture. Yes it does stretch but no where I need it to. The cut of the inner short has no contouring or cut to 'support the boys' hence wearing these command will be a no go from hear on out. Moist is a good word to describe my over all experience. The outer short is is made of a heavier but light weight material. It feels smooth, doesn't appear that it will snag and looks good. I like the pockets, drawstring and t-shirt/towel loop holder - smart design. This outer fabric has some stretch but not enough to do much more that sit...don't try yoga with these because any stretching behind that of a coach potato and you'll experience resistance in all the wrong places. I'm a true medium and these make me feel like I have more of a booty that I do. (meaning these were cut for those flat butt types - no hate, just saying).All in all - you get what you pay for. If you are on a budget, this is a no brainer, buy now! If you are not looking for any type of support for the boys with the added bonus a non-breathable fabric, look no further, these are of you! If you've got some extra case and the fertility Dr. doesn't want the boys to over head then break out that wallet and look for a name brand alternative that's 4x the price.

Title: This outfit really deserves five starts.
Review: This outfit deserves five starts, but I couldn’t give it a perfect review because there was a little bit of a mixup.First I will talk about the suit. I absolutely love it. It is very adorable and perfect for Easter for which I bought it for. The material felt really good in my hands, and Was light and airy. I got size 12 months for my son. He is a little small for his age and is just starting to fit size 12 months. The top part of the suit fits perfectly, but the pants are a little long and lose on him. All I had to do roll the waist up once and he was good to go. My son is on the short skinny side so I kind of expected that from reading all the other reviews.Now for the mixup. I ordered the classic navy. The one with the tan pants and the shirt with the anchors on it. I received the navy one. The dark gray pants and the white and blue pinstrip shirt. On my order page it said navy but when I clicked on it it came up classic navy, so I figured I was going to get the one that I wanted. When I received the wrong one I called and they rushed me out a replacement. Again on the order page it said navy but when you click on it the classic navy came up. When I told the representative this she reassured  me that I would receive the right one. The next day what do I find in my mail box. That’s right the navy on, so I called again. Once again they put in an order for the navy suit and told me that I would receive classic navy. This time I told them no I would not. I was then told that there must be something wrong with their labeling at the warehouse, and the only way to solve the problem was to open an investigation. At this point I was done I didn’t want to risk going through an investigation and not having any suit by Easter, so I just kept the suit that was sent to me. I mean I really did love the suit anyway. I just thank god I didn’t already buy the brown shoes to go with it, because now I have to buy black ones.

Title: Needed a suit quickly and this got the job done.

Although this wasn't my favorite I looked at on Amazon, I decided to order it as it was shipped directly from Amazon and would arrive in time for his First Communion.The suit looked well made (all the seams were well constructed, no loose threads or mismatched lines), but the material the suit is made out of (polyester) felt very thin. Luckily, you couldn't see thru the suit (but it sure was close!). For the price and the speed of shipment, it was worth buying. Title: Okay quality, way too big…
Review: So, I use this suit as a costume and it barely gets the job done. I’ve worn many three-piece white suits in my career as a professional Bee Gee Impersonator. Despite these pictures making the suit look pretty nice… It was way way too big for me. I ordered a size small and I definitely should’ve ordered an extra small. I was on the low end of the measurements for the small size but the discrepancy is huge. In these pictures I have completely rebuilt the entire suit with safety pins in order for it to fit like this, I took in almost 3 inches from the vest, 2 inches from the jacket and about 4 inches from the pants. Considering that this suit is coming from an Asian country I assumed it would be a smaller fit but still followed the size chart. It is quite the opposite. It is an incredibly “American” fit. It was a huge inconvenience because it took two weeks for shipping and I had a show to do. I did not have time to send the suit back and wait to get the correct size.Now I’ve worn it and put safety pins in it so I don’t think I can return it… So I’m stuck with this giant suit. If you’re using it for a costume it’s pretty OK quality. The material is a bit sheer but as you can see in the photos, it photographs well. The material and build is not great but it’s also not as bad as some other three-piece suits I’ve purchased from eBay in a similar price range. I almost gave it 2 stars but these pictures let me know it didn’t look as bad as I thought.

Title: If you saw this in a Brooks Brothers you would buy it for $90
Review: I've never done a review on a sweater because most people already know what a sweater is but this is without a doubt my new favorite sweater in my entire wardrobe, seriously.I'll probably order 2 more to store away for the future.  From my shopping experiences, I don't touch any Amazon Brands/Goodthreads/etc because it's mostly low-quality crap (sorry but that's the truth).This sweater, however, breaks that mold completely.I never expected something of this quality for under $30 shipped to my door. Every bit of the stiching, from the arms to collar to waist are impeccable and double/triple sewn for durability not just a once over like an old navy or gap piece.  Secondly, the material is high-quality and thick in a good way (not heavy enough to bake you, but it stops that cold winter wind solidly it doesn't cut through).Back to the stiching: The bear design? It's not some cheap iron-on, it's sewn through the entire sweater so I can already tell I'm never going to see any pilling/peeling/fraying but let's say 3 years down the line it does fray a little, it's the perfect style for that anyway for me because the sweater reminds of an irish cabeknit with the warm ring-collar and all.I couldn't be more pleased really, and I think I'm going to start giving Goodthreads another chance because they are definitely stepping their game up.

Title: 3 things I love and 1 thing I don't
Review: I really love this sweater! It's got some style while still delivering on extra warmth. First, I really like the draped neckline, I can get it up around the back of my neck to keep me warm. Second, I like the arms that are only tight from the elbow to the wrist - I find that I don't push the sleeves up as I do on almost everything else I own. And third, I love that it's open around my armpits. That circulation of air really feels nice and keeps me from getting overheated. Plus, I travel, so it can do double-duty as a computer/desk sweater and a going-out and looking nice sweater (though it doesn't pack particularly well - it's not that lightweight.)The only thing I don't like about it is that it seems to catch on stuff easily. The very first time I wore it, I snagged a loop on the zipper of my crossbody purse and it pulled out a big loop of thread that I can't quite get to go back in. And since it's so drapy, my pulling the loop to the inside can still show when the front comes open some. And I've noticed other small picks on it too already, so that's a bummer.But overall, I really like it, it was a great choice and I'd buy it again.

Title: A good sweater for temperate weather
Review: I bought a number of these sweaters and am quite fond of them.  They are warm enough for temperate weather, but not too warm, comfortable, soft, and loose enough not to be restrictive but not so loose as to become a baggy nuisance.  If you are looking for a casual sweater to wear over a t-shirt, I highly recommend them.  (If you have fabric sensitivities, give one a try.  I found them quite comfortable.  I did not notice them against my skin as much as I do poly blends, and I found them to breathe well and to not make me uncomfortably sweaty the way poly blends do.)The one shortcoming they may have is that they do not do all that well in the dryer.  To get around this, I let them lie flat until they are nearly dry and then just run them in the dryer for 15-20 minutes at low heat to get the last of the moisture out of them.  If you won't mind babying your cardigans in this way, then I'd recommend getting a few of these.

Title: Lovely spring sweater, TTS - instant favorite.

The V-neck is very deep so you'll need to wear something underneath, like a sportsbra. The deep V-neck means that this sweater occasionally goes 'off shoulder' for a casual, subtle, flirty element that is very fun and attractive.The material is incredibly soft! Very comfortable, easy - breezy sweater to wear. Launders easily on normal wash dry cycles. Easily dressed up or down, you'll be finding excuses to wear this sweater every chance you get - its truly that amazing.Bell sleeves terminate in a wide, elastic cuff which makes it easy to push the sleeves up allowing the bell poofs to drape over the cuff, or wear them full length. Its a versatile piece that's as easy to wear as it fun and flirty. Love it!
